stem: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his parents for evaluation of fever that has lasted 5 days.  He has been more irritable than usual and has had 3 episodes of vomiting.  The patient has no prior medical conditions and takes no medications.  He traveled internationally this year to visit his grandparents and cousins.  Immunizations are up to date.  Temperature is 38.9 C (102 F).  Physical examination shows bilateral conjunctival injection with no exudates.  The tongue is bright red and the lips are cracked.  Nonpitting edema is present on the hands and feet, and there is a maculopapular rash on the arms and legs.  Which of the following complications is this patient at greatest risk for developing?​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​​
explanation:
This patient has findings consistent with Kawasaki disease (KD), a vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that affects young children (usually age <5).  The pathogenesis is unknown but may involve a genetic predisposition (eg, Asian ancestry increases the risk) or an infection triggering systemic inflammation.

The diagnosis of KD is based on fever for ≥5 days plus 4 of the following:

  • Bilateral, nonexudative, conjunctivitis
  • Mucositis (eg, fissured erythematous lips, strawberry tongue)
  • Extremity changes (eg, edema of hands/feet, erythema of palms/soles, desquamation of fingertips)
  • Polymorphous rash
  • Cervical lymphadenopathy >1.5 cm

Although the acute symptoms of KD are self-limited, treatment (intravenous immunoglobulin) within 10 days of symptom onset is critical for reducing the incidence of complications.

Inflammation involving the coronary arteries is the most serious complication of KD, leading to coronary artery aneurysms.  Regression of aneurysms is more likely with early treatment; persistence of aneurysms increases the risk for calcification, thrombotic occlusion, or rupture.

(Choice A)  Aorta dissections are associated with long-standing hypertension and Marfan syndrome.  Inflammation of large vessels (eg, the aorta) is not seen in Kawasaki disease.

(Choice C)  Encephalitis is a complication of measles, which can present with fever, conjunctivitis, and a maculopapular rash.  However, the rash typically starts on the face, and cough, coryza, and Koplik spots (rather than strawberry tongue) are typical.

(Choice D)  Acute proliferative glomerulonephritis can occur after group A Streptococcus skin/throat infection, which may manifest as scarlet fever (eg, fever, strawberry tongue, sandpaper-textured rash).  Unlike this case, the rash in patients with acute proliferative glomerulonephritis begins in the intertriginous areas and trunk and then spreads to the extremities.  Moreover, conjunctivitis and peripheral edema would not be expected.

(Choice E)  Pulmonary cavitation typically occurs following the resolution of primary pulmonary tuberculosis.  Fever is often an initial presenting symptom, and the history may reveal exposure risk factors (eg, travel to an endemic region).  However, this patient's mucositis, conjunctivitis, and peripheral edema suggest an alternate diagnosis.

(Choice F)  Splenic rupture is a complication of infectious mononucleosis, which commonly causes fever and pharyngitis.  However, cervical lymphadenopathy is a prominent feature, not seen in this patient, and peripheral edema and conjunctivitis make this diagnosis less likely.

Educational objective:Kawasaki disease is a vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that presents with fever for ≥5 days plus conjunctivitis, mucositis, rash, extremity changes, and lymphadenopathy.  Inflammation involving the coronary arteries can lead to coronary artery aneurysms, the most serious complication of Kawasaki disease.​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌​​
